The mechanism to teach is intermediary liability: under Section 79 of the IT Act a platform keeps safe harbour only while it is a passive conduit, and the whole legal question in every deepfake case is whether recommending, monetising and generating content is still passive — which is why suits like this get filed against the platform rather than the anonymous uploader, and why a ruling here would set the terms for everyone else. Say plainly that a precedent built on a powerful complainant's case tends to produce takedown machinery that serves powerful complainants; that is the accountability angle, not the minister's grievance. Give the case particulars, the relief sought, the next hearing date, and the platforms' responses.

stories.label: CXMT: China's DRAM champion
stories.summary: CXMT rose more than 500% on its Shanghai debut to become the mainland's most valuable listed company — a memory chipmaker, not an AI model builder, taking that title. Lead with the 500% and the fact that the buyers are pricing a DRAM shortage, not a growth story: AI data centres consume memory faster than the three incumbents (Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron) add capacity, and CXMT is the first credible fourth supplier outside that oligopoly. The mechanism to teach: export controls were designed to keep China off leading-edge logic, and DRAM was the flank left open — commodity memory needs scale and capital more than it needs EUV. Who bears the cost is the surprising part and worth stating plainly: memory is the input price in every phone, laptop and server on earth, so a shortage that mints a Chinese champion also raises the price of a handset in Lagos or Lahore. Note the source spread — Seoul, Singapore, Delhi and a US wire read this event very differently (sentiment divergence 0.43); Korean coverage is reading it as a threat to Samsung and SK Hynix, Indian coverage as a consumer-price story.

stories.label: 'Can't lathicharge just because there was agitation': Supreme Court
stories.summary: The Supreme Court of India, bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant, said an agitation cannot justify police excesses or a baton charge, and will hear a batch of pleas on Tuesday alleging police violence against students protesting the exam-paper leaks. Lead with the sentence itself — 'can't lathicharge just because there was agitation' — because it is a court telling the state that disorder is not a licence. The mechanism to highlight is accountability, not sentiment: the lathi charge in India is a routine, undocumented, unreviewed use of force, and what changes if these pleas succeed is that a police commander acquires a burden of proof he has never carried. This continues our exam-leak arc (the Nilekani taskforce, the protest wind-down) but from the opposite end — that arc has been about institutional repair upstream; this is about who answers for the students who were beaten. Name the injured where the reporting names them. Follow-up hook: Tuesday's hearing, and whether the court orders any record of the force used.

stories.label: 'Fire cloud' over Bordeaux as France braces for new heatwave
stories.summary: Evacuations across France and Spain have reached 360,000 — up from the 220,000 figure we reported earlier in this arc — and a pyrocumulonimbus 'fire cloud' has formed over Bordeaux as a fresh heatwave arrives. Lead with the number and its direction of travel, then with the fire cloud, because it is the detail that carries the mechanism: a blaze large enough to build its own storm column generates its own lightning and its own wind, which is the point at which suppression stops working and the fire is only bounded by fuel and weather. Macron is holding a crisis meeting; Sánchez faces the same fires across the border. The accountability question is European civil-protection capacity — two states drawing on the same finite pool of water-bombing aircraft in the same week — not whether climate change is implicated. Follow the displaced: 360,000 people is the largest single displacement figure in this file and most of them are not tourists.

stories.label: Three killed in Benue attacks days after IGP's visit
stories.summary: At least three people killed and two injured in fresh attacks on Ohimini, Benue State — two days after Inspector-General of Police Olatunji Disu visited the state and promised 'intensified intelligence-driven operations'. Lead with the interval: two days. That gap is the story, because it converts a familiar body count into a measurable failure of a specific, named commitment by a specific, named official. The mechanism to teach a reader outside Nigeria is why Benue keeps recurring — the Middle Belt is where pastoralist routes displaced by Sahelian desertification meet settled farmland, and the state's response has been visits and pledges rather than either land adjudication or a standing security presence. Name the dead if the reporting names them, name Disu, and give the count of Benue attacks this year rather than treating this as an isolated incident. Nigeria is an OIC member and this is the sole African story in today's feed.

stories.label: Five more Palestine activists could be sentenced as terrorists
stories.summary: Five Palestine activists convicted of criminal damage in the UK face sentencing with a terrorism connection attached — and, per the reporting, were not told the case carried that connection until after they had been found guilty. Lead with that sequence, because it is the precise legal mechanism and it is checkable in the court record: a terrorism 'connection' under the Counter-Terrorism Act is a sentencing determination, not a charge, so it never has to be put to a jury and can more than double a sentence for an offence the defendants were tried for as ordinary criminal damage. The writer must verify the procedural claim against the court listing and any second outlet before publishing it as fact — Declassified UK is a single advocacy-leaning source and this is the one assertion the piece stands on. The stakes beyond these five: whether protest against an arms manufacturer is being reclassified as terrorism by a route that bypasses the jury. Name the defendants, the court and the sentencing date.

stories.label: The existential choice facing UK physics facilities: commercialize or close
stories.summary: A £42 million (US$56 million) annual hole in the finances of the UK's Science and Technology Facilities Council leaves flagship national laboratories — the Diamond Light Source among them — choosing between commercial funding and closure. Lead with the £42m, because it is small: it is roughly the cost of a mid-sized road scheme, set against instruments that took decades to build and cannot be restarted once cold. The mechanism to teach is what commercialisation actually changes at a shared facility: beam time allocated by scientific merit through open peer review becomes beam time allocated by ability to pay, and the results stop being published. Who bears the cost is the part Western coverage will miss — Diamond and ISIS serve researchers from across the Commonwealth and the Global South who have no national equivalent, and a paywalled beamline is a border. This is a funding decision presented as a technical one; name the ministers and the review that produced the shortfall.

stories.label: Argenx to buy Forte Biosciences for $2.2B
stories.summary: Argenx is buying Forte Biosciences for $2.2 billion to widen its immunology pipeline, the latest in a run of biopharma acquisitions. Lead with the ratio rather than the headline number: Forte is a clinical-stage company with no approved product, so $2.2bn is a price paid for a molecule and a patent position, not for revenue. The mechanism worth teaching an economically literate reader is why large biopharma now buys its pipeline instead of building it — internal discovery is slower and its failures are visible on the balance sheet, while an acquisition converts research risk into a one-off capital item — and what that does to drug prices, since the acquisition premium is recovered from patients over the patent term. Argenx's existing franchise is in myasthenia gravis and CIDP, rare autoimmune conditions where per-patient pricing is already extreme. State the price per share and the premium over Forte's pre-announcement close.

stories.label: ESA Ground Station in Spain Cleared to Return to Service After Wildfire Threat
stories.summary: ESA's Cebreros deep-space ground station has been cleared to return to service after inspections found the wildfires had not damaged it — Director General Josef Aschbacher announced it on 26 July. Do not write this as a wildfire story: the France/Spain evacuation piece in this cycle covers the fire itself. The subject here is that a 35-metre dish in the hills west of Madrid is one of only three stations in ESA's deep-space network, and while it was offline every mission it tracks — interplanetary probes with fixed communication windows and no ability to wait — lost coverage that has to be absorbed by New Norcia in Australia and Malargüe in Argentina. Lead with the redundancy arithmetic: three nodes worldwide, and a fire in one Spanish valley takes out a third of humanity's link to its own spacecraft. The systemic point is that scientific infrastructure sited for radio quiet is sited in dry, remote, fire-prone terrain by construction, and the fire seasons are lengthening.

stories.label: Improved inter-lab precision after CML international scale adoption: a 15-year history of BCR::ABL1 proficiency testing
stories.summary: Fifteen years of College of American Pathologists proficiency-testing data show laboratories converged on the same answer after chronic myeloid leukaemia labs adopted a common international reporting scale for BCR::ABL1. Lead with what a patient's treatment actually turns on: in CML, the decision to continue, switch or stop a tyrosine kinase inhibitor is made on log-reduction thresholds in this one measurement, so two labs disagreeing by a factor of five is two different treatment decisions for the same blood. The mechanism to teach is measurement standardisation as a public good — no new drug, no new instrument, just an agreed scale and a shared reference material, delivering an outcome improvement that a trial would have cost hundreds of millions to produce. The consequence readers should take away is where this has not happened: labs outside the CAP survey network, which is most of the world, still report on local scales, so the same patient gets a different answer in Karachi than in Chicago. State the actual precision improvement in numbers.

stories.label: How ultra-processed foods may damage your long-term brain health
stories.summary: The evidence linking ultra-processed foods to cardiovascular disease, diabetes and cancer is well established; the newer work is on the brain — depression and dementia risk. Lead with the proposed mechanism rather than the association, because associations in nutrition epidemiology are cheap and the reader knows it: the candidate pathways are gut-microbiome disruption and chronic low-grade inflammation crossing into the central nervous system, and what would distinguish them is where to look. Be explicit about the strength of evidence — 'may' is in the headline for a reason — and say what would settle it. The structural angle for our reader: UPF consumption is rising fastest not in the countries where it was studied but across the Gulf, Southeast Asia and urban Africa, where dietary transition is compressing decades of Western change into years, and the dementia burden of that arrives in the 2050s in health systems that have no capacity for it.

stories.label: US citizen charged after GrapheneOS phone wipes during airport search
stories.summary: US prosecutors have charged an Atlanta man after his GrapheneOS phone wiped itself during a border search. Lead with the fact that makes this a precedent rather than an incident: GrapheneOS has a duress mechanism and an auto-reboot timer that returns the device to a pre-first-unlock state on its own, so the wipe can occur with no action by the owner at all — which means the charge asks a court to treat a device's default security posture as the defendant's obstruction. The mechanism the reader needs is the border exception: US Customs claims authority to search devices at entry without a warrant, and the answer the security community built was not resistance but statelessness. If this prosecution succeeds, running a hardened OS becomes evidence. This is the highest-attention story in today's feed by a wide margin — 652 points and 457 comments on Hacker News — and it lands directly on our reader, who crosses borders with an encrypted phone. Name the charge and the statute.

stories.label: Bitcoin (BTC) is the canary in the coal mine for the quantum computing threat
stories.summary: 'Q-Day' is being described as a gradient rather than a date — an attacker needs only enough quantum capability to break a key before the asset behind it loses value. Lead with why Bitcoin is the early-warning system and not merely another victim: exposed public keys sit permanently on a public ledger, so the harvest step is already complete and free, and roughly a quarter of all bitcoin sits in address types whose public keys are visible now. Banks have the same cryptography but their ciphertext is not published, and they can rotate keys; a lost Satoshi-era wallet cannot. The mechanism to teach is harvest-now-decrypt-later, which applies far beyond crypto — every TLS session recorded today by a state with storage is decryptable the day the machine exists, which is why NIST's post-quantum standards matter to anyone whose government correspondence crossed a cable someone was taping. Be sceptical of the timeline claims and attribute them; the qubit counts required are still orders of magnitude away.

stories.label: Multiverse Computing Announces Series C Fundraising Targeting up to $570M (€500M) to Power Efficient AI from Edge to Cloud
stories.summary: A San Sebastián company is raising up to €500m on the proposition that the way to serve AI is to shrink the models rather than build more data centres — its method is quantum-inspired tensor-network compression, which is classical mathematics borrowed from quantum physics and runs on ordinary hardware. Lead with the contrarian bet, and be precise that nothing here requires a quantum computer; the name invites the opposite reading. Flag clearly that this is an announced target, not a closed round — the release is a GlobeNewswire wire and the number is aspirational. The structural why: every incremental watt of AI capacity currently means a data centre, a grid connection and a water allocation somewhere, and compression is the only lever that reduces all three at once. Who this matters to beyond Europe is the part worth stating — a model small enough to run on a phone is a model that works without a hyperscaler's region nearby, which is most of Africa and much of South and Southeast Asia. Name the lead investors, including the sovereign funds.

stories.label: Indonesia central bank governor Warjiyo steps down in surprise exit
stories.summary: Perry Warjiyo has resigned as governor of Bank Indonesia mid-term and without explanation, with his senior deputy Destry Damayanti installed as acting governor by a Sunday board meeting. Lead with the word 'surprise', because an unscheduled central bank departure in the world's largest Muslim-majority economy is a governance event before it is a personnel one: the rupiah is under pressure from the same oil shock that has the Fed considering a hike, and a governor who leaves in the middle of that is either being moved or is refusing to be. The mechanism to teach an economically literate reader is what central bank independence actually consists of — not a clause in a statute but a fixed term, a removal procedure with named grounds, and a successor process no president controls; Bank Indonesia has all three on paper, and the test of them is whether anyone will say why this happened. Prabowo's administration has run an expansionary fiscal programme (the free-meals scheme, the sovereign fund) that a tight monetary stance constrains, and that tension is the frame to check the reporting against — without asserting it as the cause, because nobody has established one. Who bears the cost: 280 million Indonesians, through the rupiah's import prices, and every emerging-market borrower whose risk premium moves when a peer's institutions look less predictable. Give the resignation's stated reason if any, Warjiyo's remaining term, Damayanti's standing, the appointment procedure from here, and the rupiah's and JCI's reaction. TEMPO reports it from Jakarta; CNBC and SCMP carry the market read.

stories.label: Singapore delivers back-to-back tightening to tame price risks
stories.summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore has tightened for the second meeting running, explicitly citing the Middle East conflict's effect on energy costs — a small, deliberate move announced hours before the Fed meets under pressure to hike. Lead with the instrument, because Singapore's is unique and genuinely teaches something: MAS does not set an interest rate at all, it manages the exchange rate against a trade-weighted basket, so 'tightening' means steepening the slope of a currency band. For an economy where imports and exports each exceed GDP, the exchange rate is the transmission channel that matters and the policy rate is not — which is the clearest illustration available of why an open economy's monetary tools are chosen by its trade structure, not by fashion. Follow it to the ummah-relevant point: Malaysia, Indonesia and the Gulf states face the same imported oil-and-dollar shock and have each picked a different instrument, and Singapore's is the one that trades domestic price stability for export competitiveness. Do not re-report yesterday's Fed piece — reference it in one sentence as the larger version of the same problem, and make this story about a small state acting first because it has less room to wait. Give the exact slope change, the current core inflation print, the SGD NEER reaction, and how many consecutive tightenings this now is.

stories.label: 'A new trajectory': EVs now almost quarter of Australia's new car sales as fuel crisis bites
stories.summary: Australians bought more electric vehicles in six months than in all of last year, taking EVs to nearly a quarter of new car sales, and the reporting attributes the jump to petrol-price uncertainty from the Gulf war. Lead with the causal chain, because it is the same one as the Fed and Singapore stories seen from the household end: a mined strait raises crude, crude raises pump prices, and a family in Melbourne re-prices a fifteen-year capital decision in a single quarter. The mechanism to teach an economically literate reader is that vehicle fleets turn over slowly and are therefore governed by expectations rather than by today's price — nobody switches because petrol is dear this week, they switch because they no longer believe it will be cheap for the life of the car, which is why an energy shock produces a permanent shift in demand long after the shock clears. That is the asymmetry oil exporters have historically underestimated. Follow it to who is on the other side of this: Australia has no fuel-efficiency legacy fleet policy comparable to Europe's and imports every vehicle, so the switch is a straight transfer of the import bill from refined petroleum to Chinese-built EVs and to the lithium and nickel supply chains that Indonesia is now trying to capture domestically. Give the actual percentage, the half-year unit numbers, the plug-in hybrid split, the pump price move, and what the previous trajectory looked like. Fills the Oceania gap the audit has now flagged two days running.

stories.label: At Least 2 Killed in Shooting at Food Festival in Seattle
stories.summary: Two people were killed and at least five wounded when someone opened fire at the Bite of Seattle, a food festival at the Seattle Center with thousands in attendance. Lead with the dead and the wounded — count them, name them where the authorities have, and give the trauma centre they were taken to, because the count is the fact and everything else in this story is inference. The reason it belongs in a global file rather than an American one is the mechanism visible in the response: the United States has built the finest mass-casualty trauma system in the world — Harborview is one of its flagships, and the survival rate at a shooting like this would have been unthinkable thirty years ago — and it has built it because the political system settled long ago on treating gunfire at public gatherings as a medical problem rather than a legislative one. That substitution is the transferable lesson, and it recurs wherever a state finds a harm cheaper to treat than to prevent. Resist the two easy frames: this is the only multi-source politics cluster in today's feed and it must earn its place on consequence, not on volume, so do not speculate about motive, do not reach for a national gun-policy essay, and do not write the aftermath before the investigation has produced one. Give the police account, the suspect status, the venue's security arrangements if reported, and where the four outlets' accounts of the casualty figures diverge.

stories.label: India's Cockroach Protests End as Modi Government Bows to Demands
stories.summary: The Delhi exam-leak protests have ended with the education minister gone and the government conceding the movement's demands — the first time in a decade a street movement has forced a resignation from this government. Lead with what was won and what it cost, because we have already covered the government's answer (the Nilekani task force) and the police response (pellets at Jantar Mantar); the unreported half is the movement itself. The mechanism to teach a strategic reader is how a leaderless student movement with a joke name survived long enough to extract a concession: no party sponsorship meant nothing to co-opt and nobody to arrest at the top, and a single, narrow, verifiable demand — one minister's resignation — meant the government could concede without conceding a principle. That is also the movement's ceiling, and the piece should say so plainly: nobody has been charged for the leak, nobody has been charged for the pellet injuries, the exam itself is being redesigned by a technologist rather than investigated by a prosecutor, and 2.3 million candidates still sit a test whose custody chain failed. A resignation is a scalp, not a remedy. Drop Site reports this from the ground with protesters' own accounts — use them, and keep to what it establishes. Give the minister's name and the date of the resignation, the protest's duration and peak size, the injury and arrest figures, and what the students say they will do about the unprosecuted leak. Third and final entry in this arc; do not return to it without a genuinely new development.

stories.label: Beyond the pipes -- Water infrastructure in the Global South
stories.summary: Research across cities in South Africa, India and beyond finds that urban water scarcity is not principally a question of whether pipes exist but of who reaches them, when the water flows, and who spends their day carrying it. Lead with the labour, because it is the finding and it is invisible in every infrastructure budget: where supply is intermittent, the network's shortfall is made up by unpaid household work — overwhelmingly women's and girls' — plus a borehole for those who can sink one and a tanker for those who cannot, and none of those three appear as a cost to the utility. The mechanism to teach a strategic reader is that intermittent supply is not a degraded version of continuous supply, it is a different system with a different distributive logic: pressure determines who gets water, elevation and distance from the trunk main determine pressure, and so the network's engineering silently encodes a hierarchy of neighbourhoods that no policy document ever states. That is why the per-litre price is highest at the poorest end of every one of these cities. Use this deliberately as the general case beneath two stories we ran yesterday — Karachi's single pumping station and Johannesburg's billing failure — and give it no more than a sentence each; the value here is the comparison, not a third city. Be explicit that this is academic research summarised for a general audience, not new reporting: name the researchers, the cities studied, the method, and the specific figures on collection time, tanker pricing and borehole depth that the work establishes.

stories.label: 17 flood relief camps made operational in Lahore division
stories.summary: Seventeen relief camps are open across Lahore division — in schools, at Nankana Sahib, Sharaqpur and Sheikhupura — with more sites identified in case they are needed. Lead with the camps as a measurement, because that is the only honest way to read an administrative bulletin: a commissioner's office does not open camps in advance, so seventeen operational sites is a lower bound on displacement in Punjab's most populous division, and the phrase 'more sites identified' is an official expectation that the water is still rising. The mechanism to teach a technically literate reader is why Punjab floods the way it does — this is not rainfall landing where it falls but the Ravi, Chenab and Sutlej carrying an upstream monsoon into a floodplain that has been embanked, canal-irrigated and built on for a century, so the flood peak arrives days after the rain and arrives where the engineering puts it, which is why a camp in Sheikhupura can fill on a dry morning. Add the transboundary fact our reader will want and handle it precisely: these rivers are governed by the Indus Waters Treaty and their headworks are upstream in India, so barrage releases and flood-warning telemetry are treaty obligations, not courtesies — say what the treaty actually requires on flood data and what its current operating status is, without asserting a cause for this particular peak. Who bears it: tenant farmers and katchi abadi residents on the riverine belt, the same households displaced in 2022 and 2023. Give the camp locations and capacity, the displacement and livestock figures, the river gauge readings and warning levels, and the PDMA's forecast.

stories.label: Mental and behavioral disorder-related mortality among US adolescents, 1999-2023
stories.summary: A 25-year national analysis finds mental and behavioural disorder-related deaths among US adolescents rising, with the burden falling unevenly across ethnic groups. Lead with the trend line and the disaggregation together, because a national average is exactly what this kind of study exists to break: the interesting number is never the aggregate rate but which subgroup's curve bent and when. The mechanism to teach a technically literate reader is the study's own instrument — this is death-certificate data coded to ICD-10, so what it actually measures is what a coroner wrote in a particular field, and mental-disorder-related mortality is chronically undercounted because a death from an overdose, a suicide or a complication of an eating disorder can be coded to the proximate cause instead. A rising line therefore has two candidate explanations, real increase and improved coding, and the paper's handling of that is what determines whether it is worth anything; report which it argues and on what evidence. The reason this sits in a global file: the United States has the best adolescent mortality surveillance in existence and is still arguing about what its own numbers mean, which is the strongest available caution against reading the far thinner mental-health statistics published across South Asia, the Gulf and Africa as though they described reality — a country with no psychiatric coding infrastructure reports a low rate, and that is a fact about the registry, not about its young people. Give the rates at both ends of the period, the ethnic and sex breakdowns, the ICD chapters included, and the authors' stated limitations.

stories.label: Saber-toothed cats' spinal tumors suggest inbred species struggled to survive
stories.summary: Fossil spines from the La Brea Tar Pits show saber-toothed cats carrying rare spinal nerve tumours at a rate far above anything expected in a healthy population, and the researchers read that as a signature of inbreeding in the species' final generations. Lead with the inference chain rather than the tumours, because the chain is the science: a rare disease appearing often is evidence about a gene pool, and a gene pool is evidence about population size, so a pathology in a bone becomes a demographic measurement of a species that has been extinct for eleven thousand years. The mechanism to teach a technically literate reader is the extinction vortex — as a population shrinks, deleterious recessive variants that were harmless while rare start meeting themselves, disease and deformity rise, fitness falls, the population shrinks further, and the collapse becomes self-driving well before the last animal dies. That is why conservation biologists watch effective population size rather than headcount, and it is the reason a species with several hundred individuals left can already be past saving. The second inference is the one to check hardest and the most attractive: painful spinal tumours reducing limb function would plausibly push an animal toward easy prey stuck in tar, which would mean the tar pits over-sampled the sick — so the same pathology that is the finding is also the sampling bias against it, and the paper's answer to that circularity is the test of it. Give the specimen count, the prevalence figure and its modern comparison, the dating, the institutions, and what would falsify the inbreeding reading.

stories.label: Instagram, Facebook ran AI 'nudify' ads from China, says report
stories.summary: The Tech Transparency Project reports that Meta served thousands of ads for AI 'nudify' apps — tools that generate sexualised images of real people from ordinary photographs — in breach of its own policies, placed through Beijing-based GatherOne, one of the handful of firms authorised to sell Meta inventory to Chinese advertisers. Lead with the reseller, because that is the finding and it is structural rather than accidental: Meta cannot sell ads inside China, so it delegates that market to intermediaries, and delegation moves policy enforcement from a company that answers to regulators to a company that answers to neither. The mechanism to teach a technically literate reader is the economics of ad review at scale — enforcement is a cost centre applied by classifier and sampled by humans, revenue arrives per impression whether or not the ad complies, and a channel partner is paid on the same per-impression basis, so nobody in the chain is paid to find this. That is why the violating category keeps being the one with the highest click-through. Then the consequence, which is the reason this is not a content-moderation curiosity: nudify apps are used overwhelmingly against women and girls who never consented to be photographed that way, image-based abuse is the fastest-growing category of online harm in Pakistan, India, Nigeria and across the Gulf, and in most of those jurisdictions there is no statute that names it — so the harm arrives through a platform the state cannot compel, from an app store the victim cannot reach, in a market whose ad reseller is outside every relevant law. Give the ad counts, the app names, the dates, GatherOne's role and response, and Meta's response and stated policy.

stories.label: Meet BARB, The Robot That's A Glimpse At Future Jet Engine Assembly
stories.summary: Pratt & Whitney has put a robot called BARB onto a jet engine production line — a step toward automating assembly work that has been done by hand for as long as turbofans have existed. Lead with why an incremental factory story matters this month: our Iran coverage established that the American pause in the Gulf is priced by an interceptor shortage rather than by diplomacy, which makes defence manufacturing throughput a variable in a war, and this is what a throughput fix actually looks like — not a new weapon, a robot that does not stop. The mechanism to teach a technically literate reader is why aero-engine assembly resisted automation for so long and what changed: blade-and-disc work involves compliant force control, sub-millimetre fit-up against parts with real dimensional scatter, and a certification regime in which every operation must be traceable to a person or a validated process, so the hard problem was never the arm but the qualification of the arm's output. Say which of those BARB actually solves and which it does not, because the honest answer is usually 'one station of forty'. Then the structural why for our reader: military-industrial capacity is the binding constraint of the current era, the skilled-labour pool for it is ageing across the US and Europe, and the countries buying these engines — Gulf air forces, Pakistan, Indonesia, Turkey — are trying to negotiate offsets and local assembly precisely as the work becomes less transferable, because you cannot offset a robot's job to another country's workforce. Give what BARB does, the station it replaces, the cycle-time and defect claims, and the labour numbers on that line.

stories.label: Scientists Uncover Lost ‘Golden Age’ of Languages That Ended 1,000 Years Ago
stories.summary: [Auto-backfill for tech floor] Scientists have predicted that human linguistic diversity flourished between 3,000 and 1,000 years ago, before declining with the rise of multinational states and colonial expansion.
